title: CONTRAMEM: Learning Self-Evolving Procedural Memory from Contrasting Multi-Model Trajectories

visual_explainer.blocker: No paper-grounded mechanism figure was available; the record remains text-only rather than publishing an unverified synthesis.

analysis.tldr: Contrasting heterogeneous same-task trajectories builds a transferable curated skill bank, but broader success coverage remains an alternative explanation and the offline construction bill is incomplete.
analysis.problem: Single successful trajectories omit failure, recovery, and cross-model distinctions needed for reusable procedures.
analysis.core_idea: Reflect on outcome contrasts, emit localized card deltas, and curate Function and Skill Cards through add, patch, merge, narrow, or no-op operations.

memory_design.write: Heterogeneous same-task trajectories are normalized and contrasted into procedural deltas.
memory_design.organize: A curator maintains compact Function and Skill Card banks rather than append-only logs.
memory_design.read: BM25 returns at most three cards for pre-tool guidance.
memory_design.update_forget: Offline localized curation merges or narrows cards; online update, deletion, and stale-card handling are not tested.

compared_to: No memory and self-memory in the same pipeline
Append-only memory with identical deltas and retrieval
Three matched GPT-5.5 rollouts versus heterogeneous trajectories
analysis.evidence: Held-out source-model macro success is 26.2% no-memory, 47.2% self-memory, and 55.3% shared contrastive memory; unseen Qwen rises 18.5→35.5. Under three matched trajectories, 70.0→77.5, while append-only 65.0→71.9 curated with 273→205 cards.
analysis.why_it_matters: Procedural memory quality may depend on variation across outcomes, but contrast must be separated from simply observing broader successful behavior.
limitations: The bank is frozen during target evaluation, so this is offline procedural construction rather than online self-evolution.
Twenty-three regressions include Claude Adaptability and Time slices; temporal self-memory is nearly tied.
Source generation, reflection, verifier/judge, maintenance, tokens, latency, dollars, and energy are not fully accounted.
